chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the expiation of the oath, it is a mudd, a mudd from wheat; and a handful, so that the handful is from his wheat (grain) or his oven (bread).

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A mudd, a traditional unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What is the required amount and type of food for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific measurement for expiating an oath, requiring two mudds of wheat or a handful of bread, with the latter specifically linked to the effort of grinding and fueling it. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between the raw material (wheat) and the prepared sustenance (bread), emphasizing the tangible effort and cost involved in fulfilling the vow. The hadith underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on oaths by defining the precise physical quantities required for valid expiation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>:
‘With regards to an expiation of the oath, is a handful, a handful from wheat; and the wheat can be the wheat in his grind mill or his oven’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has narrated the following:

“About the Kaffarah (expiation) due to an oath which is one mud (a certain measurement) for each person abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that it must be a handful of food made into flour and cooked.’”
